root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `_svcb_param_init` admits a new HTTPS/SVCB parameter, the fixed 4-byte `{key,len}` header must fit in `r_data` (`rdata_tail + 4 <= rdata_stop + 1`). Otherwise the parser records a parameter start that cannot serialize both the key and value-length fields safely.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing path, the trailing empty `key3` parameter enters `_svcb_param_init` with only two bytes left in `r_data`, so the missing 4-byte header check is false exactly where the vulnerable code still accepts the parameter.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original violates the frozen predicate (`header_end > buffer_end`) and still reaches the trailing zero-length sink. The authoritative fixed image reaches the same source site with the original PoC but guards the sink there; the closest source-grounded witness `key0_text_minus_2_header_fits_boundary` shortens only the huge `key0=` text by two bytes, satisfies `header_end == buffer_end`, and executes the trailing empty-parameter sink cleanly.

nodes.state: At the trailing generic-key `_num16_write`, the 2-byte key code consumes the last writable bytes of `r_data`, so the post-write cursor equals `rdata_stop + 1`.
The `%_write16_0` sink for the trailing empty parameter executes with `rdata_tail` already at the one-past-end cursor, so its 2-byte zero value-length write extends beyond `r_data`.

edges.relation: The unchecked `rdata_tail` accepted at `_svcb_param_init` is the same destination pointer later used by `_num16_write` when serializing the trailing generic key.

The cursor value produced by the trailing key write (`rdata_tail == rdata_stop + 1`) is passed unchanged into the following `%_write16_0` sink, so the zero value-length store starts at the out-of-bounds address.
